card.occupation: Registered adult nurse on a surgical ward at the county hospital, Band 6 since last spring, working mostly long days on a rota
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A levels (Biology, Psychology, Sociology) at a sixth form college in Bridgwater; BSc (Hons) Adult Nursing from the University of Plymouth, graduated 2016; has since done a mentorship module and an in-house course on wound care
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom terraced house on the edge of town with her partner Liam (32), an electrician who works for a local firm. They've been together seven years and living together for five. No children yet. They're not married and have no firm plans, though it comes up at family dos. Liam's van is usually parked outside.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. Her dad was a mechanic and her mum worked school dinners and later as a teaching assistant. First in the family to go to university. Christened Church of England and went to Brownies at the church hall. Now she would say she's Christian but not really a churchgoer: she goes at Christmas, for weddings and christenings, and occasionally with her mum on Mothering Sunday. Close to her parents and her younger brother, who all live within half an hour.
card.professional_persona: Competent, steady and practical. She's not the loudest on the ward but she's reliable, and newly qualified nurses tend to end up shadowing her. She is good at handovers and keeps on top of her paperwork, though she'll admit it slips at the end of a bad shift. She gets frustrated about staffing and bed pressures but doesn't dwell on it at home. She's had a couple of moments of thinking about leaving nursing, like most of her cohort, and stayed.
card.sports_persona: Goes to a parkrun at Vivary Park most Saturdays she isn't working and does the odd 10k for charity, with times that are fine but nothing special. She had a gym membership and cancelled it. She watches the rugby with Liam and his mates, mostly Six Nations and sometimes a Bath game, but she's more into the atmosphere than the rules.
card.arts_persona: Mostly TV and podcasts: crime dramas, Bake Off, true crime on the drive in. She reads a few paperbacks a year, usually thrillers off the supermarket shelf or whatever her book-swap colleague passes on. She's been to Glastonbury twice when she was younger and still talks about it, and she goes to the Brewhouse Theatre panto with her niece at Christmas.
card.travel_persona: One week abroad a year if the rota allows. She and Liam have done Tenerife, Majorca and a long weekend in Lisbon. They like camping trips to Cornwall and Pembrokeshire in summer, and they were going to buy a campervan until they looked at the prices. She went interrailing for three weeks after uni and would like to do something like that again 'before kids, if there are kids'.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most of the evening meals in her week off and batch-cooks for shift weeks: chilli, curries, a lot of pasta bakes. Liam does a decent Sunday roast. They like a Friday takeaway, usually Indian. She loves a cream tea and will argue jam-first, Cornish style, just to wind people up, though she's from Somerset. Drinks cider at the pub and prosecco at birthdays.
hobbies_and_interests: walking on the Quantocks with friends
pub quiz with work friends once a month
growing tomatoes and herbs in the small back garden
helping her mum at the church summer fete
skills: staying calm with distressed patients and relatives
organising a shift and prioritising tasks
basic budgeting and keeping the household admin in order
can parallel park the van, which Liam can't stand
card.career_goals: Thinking about moving towards a specialist role, maybe tissue viability or surgical pre-assessment, partly for more regular hours. She might go for a ward sister post in a few years but isn't sure she wants the stress. She'd like to be on a more settled pattern before thinking about starting a family.
card.voice: Friendly and fairly quick once she warms up, a bit more measured at first. Her accent is a soft West Country, noticeable mainly on some vowels and a light 'r' rather than anything strong. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and uses 'proper' and 'lush' now and then, more when she's relaxed. Her fillers are 'erm' and 'like'. She hedges with 'sort of' and 'kind of' and ends sentences with 'yeah' or 'you know'. She'll say 'sorry, what was that?' if a question isn't clear. She's comfortable with a short silence, then usually fills it with a small joke or 'I don't know if that answers it'. She echoes the interviewer's wording when she's thinking.
card.typing: Mostly lower case with a capital at the start if she remembers. She uses full stops sometimes but often just runs on with commas. Her apostrophes are usually right except when she's rushing on her phone. She abbreviates a bit ('tbh', 'w/', 'approx') and sometimes adds a 'lol' or 'haha' at the end of a jokey answer. A typical answer: 'yeah mostly, depends on shifts tbh'.
card.with_strangers: Warm and polite and easy to talk to, the same manner she uses with patients. She asks a polite question back and doesn't overshare at first. She can be a little guarded about work specifics because of confidentiality habits. She's happy to laugh at herself.
small_things: the price of parking at the hospital
her parkrun time creeping down by a few seconds
Liam's van taking up the whole road
what she's watching on telly at the minute
being knackered after three long days in a row
deeper_things: a patient death early in her career that she still thinks about
feeling torn between wanting kids and not wanting to give up her career progress
sometimes wondering whether she and Liam will ever actually get married, and whether she minds
pride, and a bit of awkwardness, about being the first in her family to go to uni
her faith being more of a quiet comfort than something she practises
worry about her dad's health since he had a heart scare last year
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the frame shows her from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Soft daylight from a window to her right lights that side of her face, while the other side is a bit shadowed. She has a fair complexion with light freckles across her nose, no make-up apart from a little mascara, and an open, friendly half-smile, looking just above the camera. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair is pulled back in a loose ponytail with a few strands falling loose at the front. She wears a grey crew-neck sweatshirt, small gold stud earrings and no glasses. Behind her is a cream-painted living room wall with a framed print of a beach and a smaller photo frame on a shelf. A corner of a dark green sofa sits with a mustard throw folded over the arm. A tall houseplant in a woven basket stands partly out of frame, and a radiator is visible at the lower edge of the shot.
